title: Chapter 555
paragraphs: Chapter 555
Episode 145. Premonition (24)
The recovered Octavia and the Wraith Corps fiercely pursued Jin's party.
Balkas and the swordsmen, who had agreed to take the rear, were already exhausted, but fortunately, Ron's ashen sword aura was scattered all the way to the entrance of the fortress.
Curiously enough, his sword aura did not obstruct his allies at all, it only pressured the Wraith Corps. It was as if a divine being was lending help only to those who had received its favor.
Octavia's incredible mobility was also being hindered by the ashen aura, losing its light. Thanks to this, the party was able to advance towards the fortress more easily than expected.
That's not to say they moved quickly. Giant shockwaves constantly erupted in the sky, and the ground overturned and screamed each time they set foot on it.
The battle between Ron and Kellic became even more intense, and the repercussions were felt inside the fortress as well. And most of them, Octavia and the Wraith Corps had to endure.
It was a strange formation. The Wraith Corps was acting as an umbrella, covering Jin's retreating party.
From Octavia's perspective, it was infuriating. Since the start of the ground battle, she and the Wraith Corps had continued to suffer more damage from the battle between Ron and Kellic.
'As Hedo said, it seems like he's a man favored by the heavens... His luck is endless.'
- If the heavens favor you, it's because your father has become the heavens himself.
Just as Hedo had said to Jin in the Sota Desert, Octavia felt something similar. It seemed like Jin was ridiculously lucky.

Why did the battlefield of the giants cause more damage to them, who were back to the sky? As soon as the battle began, Misha, the reinforcement, arrived at an incredibly timely moment. And even now, when they had been enhanced by the Demon Stone, they still couldn't finish it off.
Again.
Anxiety was creeping over her. A dirty premonition that they might not be able to kill Jin's party in the end was hammering in her head.
It seemed like something else would jump out from somewhere. Someone who could help Jin's party cornered.
'Damn it...!'
Even if it wasn't that someone, the fact that Balkas and the swordsmen were still not falling was terrifying.

The Black King and the swordsmen were, of course, great warriors, but they were certainly not comparable to her and the Wraith Corps. Even if they were enduring the shock of the giants, they should have taken care of them by now.
Especially the five swordsmen.
They looked no different from corpses. Their faces were so bad they looked almost black, and the swords they wielded as they retreated were not as sharp as before.

But they weren't dying. Their chests had been pierced, so this time it must be the end, their thighs had been penetrated, so their running speed must slow down, their legs were broken, so now they must fall...
They dodged all those expectations so many times that it was impossible to count.
With bodies that were almost ragged, how could they keep defending the rear while swinging their swords almost blindly, especially against her and the Wraith Corps!
Moreover, among the swordsmen, there was even one whose consciousness flickered on and off like a magic lamp every second.
The fortress was getting closer.
After the opening of the Demon Stone, the Sword Emperor Castle eventually lost most of its form.
However, the inner castle remained almost the same as it was at the beginning.
Amid the ruined buildings and broken lands, the sole intact inner castle somehow emanated a sublime aura.
It gave off the feeling that it was something precious that must be protected, even if the world was falling apart.
However, even Ron couldn't stop Octavia from directly attacking it. If Jin's party and the Phantom Legion enter the inner castle as they are, the inner castle will eventually crumble.
"You cannot pass, Jifl...."
The Sword Saints stopped their retreat in front of the inner castle. Jin and his companions paused and looked back at them.
It was evident without words.
They would buy time as a last resort, so please check Dante and, if possible, if possible… take him with you.
The back of the Sword Saints said so. There was no one among them who could survive even if they received treatment right now, it said so.
Sacrifice, truly dreadful.
"That's right, a correct choice... but now it's going to be really hard to make sense."
Octavia spoke in a low voice soaked in hatred. She and the Phantom Legion pointed their staves at the Sword Saints.
Indeed, the miracles of the Sword Saints, which had been happening hundreds of times up until now, were about to end here.
Jin turned around and walked toward the Sword Saints, drawing his Thunderbolt Sword, Siegmund.
'My lord....!'
'Lord!'
His companions felt the same. They too did not want to trample on the sacrifice of their comrades and move on.
But they had to judge calmly. This was clearly what the Sword Saints did not want. They also felt Jin's approaching energy and wanted to scream for him to just leave.
That's why his companions had to stop Jin, but Jin was not just moving towards the Sword Saints because his heart ached and he lost his reason.
Wouldn't he step forward even in this situation?
To ask Runcandel, his own clan, that question.
'Whoever came from the clan. If I fight here, even spreading the Sovereign Domination Sword, they know that not only the Sword Saints will die.'
It was a kind of threat, and as always.
Jin was able to achieve what he wanted.

As Octavia and the Phantom Legion's magic poured onto the Sword Saints, and Jin's companions tried to forcibly pull him back, a group of knights who had been hiding in the barrage stood in front of Jin and the Sword Saints. There were five Black Knights.
'Again, really again...!'
Octavia gritted her teeth and glared at the Black Knights.
-Do you think Runcandel will step in to save me, Octavia Jifl?
-Certainly. Now you have reached such a position in Runcandel.
Just as she had a conversation with Jin as soon as they faced each other on the ground, in fact, Octavia had been considering Runcandel's support from the beginning.
Even so, the reason they were now astonished was simply that they were fed up.
They couldn't help but feel their blood boiling at the fact that Jin always managed to create a situation that was advantageous to him.
Swoosh-!
The knights' swords cut through Octavia and the phantoms' magic. They must have endured the power of the giants while following the group, but they showed no signs of exhaustion.
On the contrary, the powerful sword energy that blocked the path in front of the inner castle was stronger than any active black knight Jin had ever seen.
Jin's companions could finally feel relieved, and Jin's fighting spirit subsided a little.
It was a tactical decision, knowing that the black knights would never step forward if Jin didn't show the will to fight alongside the swordsmen.
"12th generation."
The calm and heavy voice of Stamm echoed without losing its energy in the roar of the battle.
Jin had never heard Stamm's voice directly and did not know his position, but he instinctively knew that he was the captain of the Rune Candle black knights.
"You always have the talent to surprise the members of the family in this way."
Stamm's sword emitted a fierce resonance, pushing away the surrounding energy. As soon as he appeared, Octavia and the phantoms had no choice but to change their formation from pursuit to battle.
"Stamm... did Rosa Runecandel not come herself?"
Stamm did not answer Octavia and looked back at Jin's group. He seemed to have no problem with the phantoms being in front of him.
For a few seconds, Stamm's gaze lingered on Jin's group and the unbroken inner castle. Finally, it settled on the broken swordsmen.
As a warrior and a human.
It was a landscape that could only be admired.
"Thanks to the 12th generation, I am grateful to be able to pay tribute to you. It is an honor to help you in your final moments, although it was not my intention."
As a warrior, he was moved by them and wanted to help them as a human, but for the black knights, their primary mission and the interests of the family came first.
So, although it was not quite appropriate to step forward now, it was inevitable considering Jin's injury or death.
"...Sir Stamm, I promise you. The day will come when Hyran repays your kindness. Even if a thousand years pass."
Even with Stamm and the black knights' appearance, the swordsmen's deaths were already inevitable.
Jin knew this fact as well. He had forcibly involved the family because it was necessary. He knew better than anyone that, realistically, the swordsmen's power alone could not buy much time.
Stamm nodded and made eye contact with Jin.
"Go, 12th generation."
Jin did not ask Stamm to make time for them to say their last goodbyes to the swordsmen.
From the moment the battle on the surface began, Jin and his companions had been saying their farewells to the swordsmen all along.
The battle itself was no different from a long farewell for them.
Jin and his companions took one last look at the swordsmen's backs and turned their bodies back toward the inner castle.
Octavia could not capture them as they left.
"A while ago, Octavia Ziefl asked if Rosa did not come herself."
Stamm added, pointing his sword.
"It would be wise to be grateful that Rosa sent me in her place."
Stamm's voice, filled with contempt, pierced Octavia's lungs.
Dante Hyran.
Amidst the inner war between the white stone and the fields, he walked endlessly along the gray path.
He couldn't remember how much time had passed, why he was here, what he was resisting... Such things didn't come to mind anymore.
Am I doing well...?
He clearly remembered the fact that he had been in a fierce battle. The fact that he had waged a struggle so intense that it couldn't be expressed in words.
But now it was peaceful.
The tempting voice that, for some reason, he felt he should never follow, could no longer be heard.
I'm doing well. And, I have overcome...
As soon as such feelings sprouted like horns, his footsteps became lighter. He didn't know what he had won against, but it seemed that if he kept walking, something good would happen.
As he continued through the gray area for a while, Dante could hear a new voice.
Dante...!
Dante!
It was not the tempting voice that he felt he should never succumb to, but a completely different, very familiar, and well-known one.
It was the voice of a friend.
'Jin!'
Dante started running towards the direction where Jin's voice was coming from, with a wide smile on his face.
Before he went too far, the voice came closer, and a door appeared out of nowhere on the gray land.
He quickly touched the door.
'But, is it alright to open it and leave...?'
Suddenly, a sense of inexplicable anxiety seeped into his excited heart.
Dante!
His friend's urgent voice rang out again, and Dante stopped hesitating and opened the door.
As soon as he left through the door, the white stone looked at the wide-open door and thought:
Finally.
I can leave.
